description:
Hello we are the team of Hope and Ambition

We are from UAE and we are currently in grade 12

Our team consists of: 2 Emiratis, 1 Jordanian, and 1 Sudanese

We are designing a story about equipment left on the moon, on mars, and in deep space.
summary:
The Machines That Remain is an interactive children’s storybook that brings NASA’s past space hardware back to life. Children follow Leo, a curious young explorer, as he meets Sojourner, Opportunity, InSight, and Voyager 1 through animated scenes and friendly conversations.

Each chapter combines creative storytelling with accurate NASA science. Children learn that Sojourner was the first wheeled vehicle used on another planet, Opportunity found evidence of ancient water on Mars, InSight listened for marsquakes, and Voyager 1 became the first human-made object to enter interstellar space.

By presenting real missions as a visual adventure instead of a technical information page, the project helps young audiences understand how engineering creates scientific discovery. It also shows that even when a spacecraft stops operating, the knowledge it gathered continues to inspire future exploration.
details:
The Machines That Remain is an interactive animated digital storybook for children ages 7–12. The story follows Leo, a curious child who receives a mysterious message from space and travels to meet four NASA explorers: Sojourner, Opportunity, InSight, and Voyager 1.

Instead of presenting mission facts as a long technical list, the project teaches science through character dialogue, speech bubbles, illustrated scenes, gentle animations, and short story chapters. Each explorer explains its purpose and shares one important scientific discovery or achievement in a child-friendly way.

The website was created using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in a single responsive webpage. It includes animated chapter transitions, interactive dialogue, a restart button, a science clue for each mission, and a sources section based on NASA and NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory resources.

The project is creative because it transforms historical space hardware into memorable characters while keeping the scientific information accurate. It is designed to make children feel emotionally connected to robotic explorers and inspire curiosity about space science, engineering, and future exploration.
